item.title: Thriving exchanges add new momentum to China-Botswana partnership
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-12
Thriving exchanges add new momentum to China-Botswana partnership A drone formation depicts an elephant and a panda during a drone light show in Gaborone, Botswana, on Sept. 8, 2026. (Xinhua/Tshekiso Tebalo) GABORONE, Oct. 11 (Xinhua) -- Botswanan President Duma Gideon Boko will pay a state visit to China from Oct. 12 to 17 at the invitation of Chinese President Xi Jinping, as the two countries seek to deepen cooperation in trade, investment and people-to-people exchanges. In January 2025, Xi and Boko exchanged congratulations on the 50th anniversary of diplomatic ties, expressing confidence in the prospects for closer cooperation. In September 2024, the two countries elevated their bilateral ties to a strategic partnership. Beyond these diplomatic milestones, cooperation between both countries has taken shape in projects ranging from energy and mining to education and health care. IMPROVING LOCAL LIVELIHOODS Chinese-invested companies have maintained steady cooperation with Botswana for years, covering areas such as infrastructure, energy and mining, bringing tangible benefits to local communities. Water infrastructure projects have helped improve access to essential services across Botswana. The Thune Dam, constructed by Chinese companies, supplies water for domestic and agricultural use, with its water resources integrated into Botswana's North-South Water Carrier system. Other projects, including water supply and sanitation works in Maun and the Boteti region, are also helping improve local water services. Meanwhile, the Digital Delta Data Center is strengthening Botswana's digital infrastructure and supporting the growth of its digital economy. Cooperation in energy and mining is creating further opportunities for development. The Jwaneng 100 MW Solar Power Plant project has officially commenced operations, helping to ease Botswana's electricity shortage and strengthen the country's energy security. Meanwhile, the Khoemacau Copper Mine Expansion Project is expected to boost production and generate employment opportunities. The establishment of the Mining Centre of Excellence at Maun Technical College with the support of Botswana's Ministry of Higher Education also helps equip young people with practical skills tailored to the needs of the mining industry, linking vocational training more closely with local employment. Beyond economic development, cooperation has also extended to healthcare and education. The teaching hospital at the University of Botswana School of Medicine in Gaborone supports medical care and training, while four China-aided primary schools have improved learning conditions for local children, contributing to the development of Botswana's basic education system. Students enjoy leisure time after school at China-aided Mmopane Primary School in Mmopane, Kweneng District, Botswana, Nov. 4, 2024. (Xinhua/Han Xu) EXPANDING TRADE, DEEPENING COOPERATION Economic and trade cooperation between China and Botswana is mutually beneficial and enjoys broad prospects. Bilateral business trips and engagements have become increasingly frequent, with continued exchange between the two sides. From May 1 this year, China extended zero-tariff treatment to all 53 African countries with which it has diplomatic ties, bringing significant benefits to Botswana's premium products, such as beef and citrus. "This important initiative opens new opportunities for Botswana to expand its exports, strengthen trade and deepen our economic cooperation with China," said Botswana's Minister for State President, Defense and Security Moeti Mohwasa. Two-way trade between China and Botswana reached 1.222 billion U.S. dollars in 2025, an increase of 21.3 percent year on year, and rose by 58.6 percent to 852 million U.S. dollars in the first half of 2026 compared with the same period last year, official statistics showed. In January 2021, the two countries signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) for cooperation on the Belt and Road Initiative, making Botswana the 46th African partner country to join the initiative. In 2025, the two countries signed a MoU on promoting the implementation of the Global Development Initiative, and Botswana joined the Initiative on International Trade and Economic Cooperation Framework for Digital Economy and Green Development. These bilateral agreements provide new opportunities, expand cooperation into new sectors, and open up new prospects for China-Botswana practical cooperation. Chinese Ambassador to Botswana Fan Yong (2nd R) and Botswanan Vice President and Minister of Finance Ndaba Gaolathe (2nd L) sign an agreement on economic and technical cooperation between the two governments in Gaborone, Botswana, Feb. 27, 2025. (Photo by Tshekiso Tebalo/Xinhua) Many Chinese business delegations have visited Botswana to explore market opportunities, while Botswana's officials and think tank representatives have praised the achievements of Chinese modernization following visits to China. Viewing China as "a constant friend and a reliable development partner," Botswana seeks to learn from China's achievements in improving people's living standards and poverty alleviation, as the southern African country pursues its own development agenda, seeking investment, partnerships, and alignment between development strategies. BRINGING PEOPLE CLOSER People-to-people exchanges have brought the two peoples closer through cultural, educational and community activities, including "Chinese Bridge" competitions, film festivals and medical outreach programs by Chinese medical teams. The Confucius Institutes at the University of Botswana in Gaborone and the Botswana International University of Science and Technology (BIUST) in Palapye in central Botswana run programs on promoting Chinese language education and cultural exchange. "By learning the Chinese language, our students gain a key to unlocking opportunities in a rapidly globalizing world," said BIUST Vice Chancellor Otlogetswe Totolo, describing the institute as a platform for cultural exchange, academic collaboration and closer friendship between Botswana and China. The growing popularity of the Chinese language and culture among the people of Botswana has helped strengthen people-to-people ties and deepen bilateral friendship, while more Botswana people are looking forward to opportunities to visit China. "The relationship between Botswana and China has grown steadily over many decades, bringing cooperation for many, many years of mutual interests," said Botswana's Minister of International Relations Phenyo Butale. Over the years, bilateral partnership in the health sector has continued to flourish. Since 1981, 18 successive groups of Chinese medical professionals, comprising more than 600 experts in total, have traveled thousands of miles to serve in Botswana. They have become an integral part of Botswana's healthcare system, providing specialized medical care to local communities and strengthening bilateral cooperation. Luo Jinying (R), chief obstetrician with the 17th batch of the Chinese medical team to Botswana, conducts Doppler ultrasound examination for a local pregnant woman at Princess Marina Hospital in Gaborone, Botswana, May 5, 2026. (Xinhua/Yang Guang) "Their dedication has significantly improved access to specialized healthcare, enhanced the quality of medical services, strengthened the capacity of our healthcare system, and ultimately contributed to improving the health outcomes of our people," said Tshepo Machacha, acting permanent secretary of Botswana's Ministry of Health. Machacha himself has received traditional Chinese acupuncture therapy. He said traditional Chinese medicine has enriched Botswana's healthcare system. "This serves as a practical demonstration of how cultural exchange and medical cooperation can directly improve patient care while strengthening medical understanding between the two nations," he said. item.title: High-frequency data points to China's improving economic momentum in Q3
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-12
High-frequency data points to China's improving economic momentum in Q3 This photo taken with a mobile phone on Oct. 1, 2026 shows tourists at a local tea house in Haikou, south China's Hainan Province. (Xinhua/Guo Cheng) BEIJING, Oct. 11 (Xinhua) -- China's economy continued to improve in the third quarter of this year, with new growth drivers gaining momentum, official high-frequency data on consumption, trade and investment showed Sunday. Consumer activity continued to recover, with offline consumption payments up 2.6 percent year on year in the third quarter, accelerating by 0.7 percentage points from the second quarter, according to data released by the State Information Center under the National Development and Reform Commission. In September, offline consumption payments increased 3.1 percent from a year earlier, up 0.5 percentage points from August, marking three consecutive months of growth. The data also showed that the weight carried by cargo ships departing from and arriving at major Chinese ports rose 43.1 percent and 0.3 percent year on year, respectively, in the third quarter. On investment, the issuance of new special-purpose bonds rose 50.2 percent year on year in September, 43.6 percentage points faster than the August level, the data showed. The value of contracts awarded for projects related to new infrastructure, including computing power, data and networks, increased 34.2 percent year on year in the third quarter and 50.4 percent year on year last month. Capital investment in frontier sectors such as artificial intelligence and humanoid robots surged 184.1 percent year on year in the third quarter and 198.7 percent year on year in September, the data showed. "Investment in frontier fields such as artificial intelligence has remained strong, supporting current growth while building momentum for the development of new quality productive forces," said Wei Ying, deputy director of the center's big data development department. China has targeted 2026 growth at 4.5 to 5 percent and will strive for even better results in practice. In the first half of the year, the country's gross domestic product grew 4.7 percent year on year. In another sign of a firming economy, China's manufacturing activity returned to expansionary territory in September, while non-manufacturing activity rebounded markedly. The purchasing managers' index for China's manufacturing sector stood at 50.1 last month, while the business activity index for the non-manufacturing sector reached 50.2. item.title: Long March legacy inspires innovation breakthroughs in city of historic turning point
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-12
Long March legacy inspires innovation breakthroughs in city of historic turning point People visit the Zunyi Meeting memorial hall in Zunyi City, southwest China's Guizhou Province, Aug. 17, 2026. (Photo by Zhang Zhengju/Xinhua) ZUNYI, Guizhou, Oct. 11 (Xinhua) -- Lei Guangren has crossed the weathered stone arch bridge countless times in Zunyi, a city in southwest China's Guizhou Province. Known as Yinghong Bridge, or "Welcoming the Red Army Bridge," it bears quiet witness to the Chinese Red Army's epic Long March more than nine decades ago. Such Long March-associated place names pepper every corner of the mountainous city, earning Zunyi its resonant title: the "city of historic turning point." "The Zunyi Meeting, held here during the Long March, marked a life-or-death turning point in the history of the Communist Party of China (CPC)," said Lei, 78, former curator of the Zunyi Meeting memorial museum. "From then on, the Party found the right direction and leadership, stayed the course toward its goals, defeated the enemies and embarked on a path of independence and self-reliance." The year 2026 marks the 90th anniversary of the victory of the Long March. Lei believes the spirit of what American journalist Edgar Snow described as "an odyssey unequaled in modern times" continues to inspire China as it pursues its Second Centenary Goal. In October 1934, the CPC was forced to retreat from the Central Soviet Area in east China's Jiangxi Province and move northwest after enduring a series of encirclement campaigns by rival forces of the Kuomintang party (KMT). The CPC-led Red Army fought its way across the Xiangjiang River in Guangxi and broke through the KMT troops' blockade, but suffered tens of thousands of casualties in the battle. In downtown Zunyi stands a two-story gray-and-white building where Lei had worked for a decade. In January 1935, at a critical historical crossroads, the Zunyi Meeting was held in this building, establishing Mao Zedong's leading position in the CPC Central Committee and the Red Army in practice. The spirit of the Zunyi Meeting -- characterized by firm conviction, commitment to truth, independence and self-reliance, and unity -- continues to resonate today. In his book "The Long March: The Untold Story," American journalist and author Harrison Salisbury wrote that China's course "had been set for at least half a century to come." Tourists visit the historical site of the Zunyi Meeting in Zunyi City, southwest China's Guizhou Province, Oct. 1, 2026. (Photo by Tian Jinhong/Xinhua) The Red Army subsequently won its first major victory since the start of the Long March at Loushan Pass in northern Zunyi and later broke out of enemy encirclement through its four crossings of the Chishui River. "My mother told me that she was working when Red Army soldiers passed by our home. They borrowed a douqiang to shelter from the rain," Lei recalled. A douqiang is a bamboo-woven tool traditionally used in southern China for drying grain. By the time the rain stopped, the soldiers had already reached the neighboring village. Before leaving, however, they asked local residents to make sure the tool was returned to Lei's mother. Salisbury's book also mentions Kong Xianquan, a Red Army soldier who led troops in an assault during the Battle of Loushan Pass. Hit by six bullets in the hip, Kong was left behind in Guizhou to recover from his wounds. After the founding of the People's Republic of China, he helped establish the Zunyi Meeting memorial museum and became its first curator. Today, his granddaughter Kong Xia has spent more than three decades sharing stories of China's revolutionary history. "In Zunyi, stories of the Red Army are passed down like family heirlooms, reminding each new generation not to forget where we came from or where we are going," she said. For 56-year-old Kong, Zunyi is a city where tradition and modernity coexist. Xiaolongshan, where some Red Army martyrs were buried, was renamed Hongjunshan, or Red Army Mountain. Year after year, visitors come to pay tribute here beside a bronze statue of a Red Army soldier draped in red silk by local residents. Beyond these landmarks, a 10-minute walk from the site of the Zunyi Meeting stands the theater for "The Great Turning Point," a large-scale immersive production about the Long March, where history is retold through live performance. Chen Jinghong, a visitor from southwest China's Chongqing Municipality, brought her 10-year-old daughter to see the show. "It is like planting a seed in a child's heart, allowing her to experience the culture of the Long March and gradually understand and appreciate it as she grows up," Chen said. But Zunyi is far more than a museum of revolution. It has undergone dramatic transformation. When the Red Army passed through, its population stood at just over 30,000. By 2025, the permanent population of its central urban area exceeded 1.6 million, with an urbanization rate of 61 percent. An aerial drone photo taken on July 31, 2026 shows the Huajiang Grand Canyon Bridge in southwest China's Guizhou Province. (Xinhua) And it is not just Zunyi that has developed. Guizhou, a mountainous province with no natural plains, has emerged as a "museum of bridges." Nearly half of the world's tallest bridges stand here. "The Long March in Guizhou was about breaking through encirclement and relying on one's own strength," Kong said. "Today, we are far removed from the smoke of war, but in science and technology, we are also making breakthroughs." One striking example is the Huajiang Grand Canyon Bridge in Guizhou. Holding world records both as the highest and the longest-span steel truss girder suspension bridge located in mountainous terrain, it has been dubbed by Chinese internet users a bridge that is "world No. 1, both horizontally and vertically." Its main cables and upper structural components were produced by Guizhou Wire Rope Co., Ltd. The core steel wires were both developed and manufactured in Guizhou, forming a critical lifeline for the project. "Wire-rope production used to be dominated in many areas by European and American companies. After the efforts of several generations, our products are now widely used in major equipment across land, sea and air, helping overcome technological bottlenecks," said Yang Zhengyan, director of a product research and development office at Guizhou Wire Rope. At Laoyashan, where fierce fighting involving the Red Army once took place, bullet marks can still be seen on the rocks. At the foot of the mountain lies the old factory compound of Guizhou Wire Rope. It was there that Yang and his team conducted countless tests to develop a mooring cable for offshore engineering. Such cables had previously been expensive and required long procurement cycles, posing constraints on the development of China's offshore oil and gas resources. "There is no room for failure with a product like this, so for many tests that would normally have been conducted only once, we ran them over and over again. We also pioneered some testing methods," Yang said. In August 2023, the first permanent mooring cable for a floating production, storage and offloading unit, or FPSO, developed by Guizhou Wire Rope, was successfully deployed in the mooring system of the "Nanhai Fenjin" FPSO. It marked China's first application of a domestically produced permanent mooring cable for an FPSO, ending the country's long-standing reliance on foreign products in this field. The group is now capable of mass-producing the cable. It can be used not only for deep-sea oil production platforms, but also for offshore wind power platforms. The system can reduce the sea area occupied by conventional mooring systems to about one-tenth, while also reducing their environmental footprint. "The spirit of the Long March tells me to find the right direction, not to act blindly, and not to fear hardship or failure," said Yang, a 46-year-old Guizhou native. This photo taken on Aug. 17, 2026 shows a view of Loushan Pass in Zunyi City, southwest China's Guizhou Province. (Xinhua/Shi Qiangui) For another Zunyi native, 52-year-old Lin Guojun, chairman of Shenzhen Busbar Sci-Tech Development Co., Ltd., the city has also played an important role in his company's growth. Busbar holds more than 580 patents and international certifications, with its products used in new energy vehicles, wind power, solar power, smart grids and other new energy industries. "We began developing our new energy business in 2008. It was an attempt to overtake on a curve," Lin recalled. "Back then, we had neither a market nor the technology, and the world did not believe China could develop a new energy industry." In 2012, when the company encountered difficulties and struggled to fulfill orders, Lin turned his attention to Zunyi. "Some of our equipment would shut down when temperatures became too high. Zunyi has a favorable natural environment, supporting industries, access to many major surrounding cities, and supportive policies," said Liu Yong, production and operations manager of Zunyi Busbar Sci-Tech Development Co., Ltd. A new factory was completed in just seven months. Inside the plant, many production processes are semi-automated, with more than 40 robots and robotic arms operating in an orderly fashion to ensure greater consistency in product quality. The Zunyi facility now focuses on developing and manufacturing high-voltage system components for new energy vehicles, including charging connectors, charging piles, high-voltage relays and high-voltage wiring harnesses. Its products are supplied directly to domestic and overseas automakers. Lin, who grew up listening to stories about the Red Army, said he sees parallels between the Long March and his own industry. "From a time when China's new energy sector was little known globally to today, when Chinese new energy vehicles have won worldwide recognition, our work in this industry has itself been a breakthrough," he said. "It takes perseverance and conviction to see something like this through." Tourists experience VR devices at the Zunyi Meeting memorial hall in Zunyi City, southwest China's Guizhou Province, Oct. 1, 2026. (Photo by Yuan Fuhong/Xinhua) China's 15th Five-Year Plan, released in the first half of this year, sets out comprehensive arrangements for accelerating high-level self-reliance and strength in science and technology and fostering new quality productive forces. Among its seven major economic and social development goals for 2026-2030 is substantially boosting the country's capacity for independent innovation. Zunyi's government work report this year also called for developing new quality productive forces in light of local conditions and accelerating the building of a modern industrial system. The national vision also plays out in ordinary people's lives. Kong is thinking of replacing her family's gasoline car with a new energy vehicle. A frequent traveler across China, she recently took a high-speed train to Yan'an. The trip, which once took the Red Army nine months, now takes less than nine hours. Her 27-year-old son Jiang Xiao carries the legacy forward as part of a youth lecture group, sharing stories of the Long March. "Every generation has different experiences and its own interpretation of the Long March spirit," Kong said. "Yet the spirit never fades with time, and these stories deserve to be passed on." item.title: Zheng Qinwen claims maiden WTA 1000 title at China Open
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-12
Zheng Qinwen claims maiden WTA 1000 title at China Open Zheng Qinwen poses with the trophy during the awarding ceremony after the women's singles final between Zheng Qinwen of China and Mirra Andreeva of Russia at 2026 China Open tennis tournament in Beijing, China, Oct. 11, 2026. (Xinhua/Sun Fei) BEIJING, Oct. 11 (Xinhua) -- China's Zheng Qinwen captured the women's singles title at the 2026 China Open on Sunday, defeating fourth-seeded Russian Mirra Andreeva 7-5, 6-4 in the final to claim her maiden WTA 1000 crown before breaking down in tears during an emotional celebration on home soil. "The feeling is incredible. Winning here in Beijing, in front of my home crowd, has always been one of my dreams," Zheng said after the match. The victory also made Zheng the first Chinese player to win the singles title at the China Open. "Today's match was extremely tough. Mirra is a great player, and she broke my serve right at the start," Zheng said. "I just had to take it one point at a time and keep telling myself to hang in there and never give up. After playing so many matches, I was physically and mentally exhausted. But playing in front of my home crowd gave me that extra strength to keep pushing through." "I want to congratulate Mirra on her outstanding achievement at Roland Garros this year. I never had a chance to congratulate you in person, so I want to do that now. Congratulations on reaching the final this week as well. You are such a young and talented player, and congratulations to you and your team on everything you've achieved," she added. Since winning Olympic gold at the Paris 2024 Games, a persistent right elbow injury has disrupted Zheng's career and required surgery in July 2025. Her ranking subsequently fell from a career-high No. 4 in 2024 to as low as No. 160 in mid-June 2026. "I want to thank my team for supporting me throughout this journey. I've been through a very tough year, and I couldn't have done this without you. Last but not least, I want to thank all the sponsors, the referees, and all the staff who have worked so hard throughout the week. And thank you to all the fans for your incredible support. This title belongs to all of you, too!" The victory earned Zheng 1,000 ranking points and 1,151,380 U.S. dollars in prize money, lifting her to No. 23 in the live WTA rankings. item.title: Xi leads efforts toward building Healthy China
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-12
Xi leads efforts toward building Healthy China BEIJING, Oct. 11 (Xinhua) -- On a small island in the Yangtze River in eastern China, residents don't need to leave the island to see a medical specialist. They can now access modern medical equipment at the township clinic and consult specialists from higher-level hospitals, who pay regular visits to the facility. In December 2014, Chinese President Xi Jinping visited the clinic in Shiye Township, Jiangsu Province, outlining a path for advancing rural healthcare. Shiye is home to five villages and more than 10,000 permanent residents. "We must shift the focus of healthcare to the community level, channel more medical resources to local communities, and promote equal access to basic public services in urban and rural areas," said Xi, who is also general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission. This is to provide people with safe, effective, accessible and affordable public health services and basic medical care, and effectively address the difficulties and high costs people face in accessing medical care at the local level, he added. Since the 18th CPC National Congress in late 2012, the Party Central Committee, with Xi at the core, has given strategic priority to ensuring people's health. It made the major decision to advance the Healthy China Initiative nationwide. From targeted advances in key areas to nationwide coverage of inclusive health services that meet basic needs, China, a country of more than 1.4 billion people, has blazed a path of inclusive and balanced health development. HEALTHCARE FOR ALL Over the years, Xi has visited grassroots medical institutions and households in rural areas across the country, offering targeted guidance tailored to local conditions. He has focused on preventing people from falling into or returning to poverty because of illness, using remote consultations to help balance medical resources, and addressing healthcare-related issues in rural areas. Xi has paid close attention to the issues people face in accessing healthcare at the grassroots level and set out clear directions, from establishing five basic systems -- tiered diagnosis and treatment, modern hospital management, universal medical insurance, drug supply security, and comprehensive oversight -- to developing the healthcare workforce and digital infrastructure for smart healthcare. "We must unswervingly uphold the public welfare nature of the medical and healthcare sector, and not take the path of wholesale marketization and commercialization," Xi said. He has also called for further deepening the reform of medical and healthcare systems and exploring Chinese solutions to the worldwide challenge of healthcare reform. Coordinated development and governance of healthcare services, medical insurance and pharmaceuticals have helped reduce out-of-pocket payments to 27.1 percent of total health expenditure. The vision of ensuring that serious illnesses can be treated within one's province, common illnesses within one's city or county, and everyday ailments at the grassroots level is increasingly becoming a reality. China has supported the development of 125 national regional medical centers so far, with 75 percent of their hospitals located in central and western regions and other areas where high-quality medical resources are relatively scarce. More than 90 percent of residents can access nearby medical and healthcare services within 15 minutes. Primary-level medical institutions account for more than 50 percent of all medical visits nationwide. COMPREHENSIVE LIFECYCLE HEALTH Xi has also expressed deep concern over the growing prevalence of myopia among students, particularly at younger ages. The trend, he has said, seriously affects children's health and poses a major issue for the future of the country, and it must be given high priority and not allowed to continue unchecked. With strengthened efforts to prevent and control myopia among children and adolescents, China's overall student myopia rate declined for five consecutive years from 2021 to 2025, reaching 49.9 percent in 2025, down 3.7 percentage points from 2018. From enabling older people to enjoy their later years to preventing childhood obesity and myopia, Xi has stressed the importance of safeguarding health across all population groups and throughout the entire lifecycle. A range of health indicators point to improvements in the country's overall health status. In 2025, China's average life expectancy rose to 79.25 years, while its major health indicators remained at the leading position among upper-middle-income countries and countries with a population exceeding 100 million. The premature mortality rate from major chronic diseases fell to 13.8 percent, and major infectious diseases and endemic diseases were brought under effective control. China aims to establish a health system by 2035 that is compatible with a society that has basically achieved modernization. Xi has emphasized the translation of scientific and technological innovations into practical applications, called for advancing the digital and intelligent development of healthcare nationwide, and encouraged regions with suitable conditions to explore the application of artificial intelligence. This year, the government work report included biomedicine as an emerging pillar industry for the first time. In the first half of 2026 alone, China approved 38 innovative drugs for market entry. China is developing a growing range of homegrown drugs, medical equipment, vaccines, medical consumables and approaches to diagnosis and treatment. Traditional Chinese medicine is a distinctive component of China's healthcare system. Xi has issued important instructions on multiple occasions, calling for the sector's industrial development and modernization, as well as wider international reach. China has also continued to deepen health cooperation with countries around the world by promoting the use of artemisinin to benefit patients worldwide, regularly deploying medical teams abroad, establishing overseas traditional Chinese medicine centers, and joining efforts to combat Ebola. Through these efforts, it has worked with other countries to address cross-border public health risks. Yet as China's economy and society evolve and its demographic landscape changes, people's healthcare needs are becoming increasingly multi-layered and diverse. "At present and for a period to come, China's health and healthcare work needs to adapt to changing circumstances and refine certain specific policies and measures. However, the path of health and healthcare development with Chinese characteristics must not waver," Xi said. Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. All Rights Reserved.

item.title: Commentary: Taiwan leader's repackaged rhetoric cannot conceal his secessionist agenda
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-11
Commentary: Taiwan leader's repackaged rhetoric cannot conceal his secessionist agenda BEIJING, Oct. 10 (Xinhua) -- Taiwan leader Lai Ching-te reiterated his secessionist agenda and stoked cross-Strait tensions in a speech in Taipei on Saturday, using carefully crafted rhetoric to mislead the Taiwan public and sway international opinion. Once again, he invoked "democracy" to sensationalize the so-called "mainland threat" and promote a false narrative of "democracy versus authoritarianism." Such rhetoric seeks to exploit the concept of democracy to justify secessionism. The Taiwan question originated from a civil war fought between the forces led by the Communist Party of China (CPC) and the Kuomintang (KMT) about eight decades ago. In 1949, the defeated KMT retreated to Taiwan, while the People's Republic of China was founded under the leadership of the CPC. The unresolved civil war and foreign interference have left the two sides of the Taiwan Strait in a prolonged state of political confrontation. However, the fact that Taiwan is an inalienable part of China's territory has never changed. Both history and reality make clear that Taiwan's future should be jointly decided by all Chinese people, including Taiwan compatriots. Differences in political systems are neither an obstacle to China's reunification nor an excuse for splitting the country. Lai said he would "never allow the distortion of World War II history." Yet his own words have repeatedly distorted history and undermined the outcomes of WWII. Lai refused to say a word about China's victory in the War of Resistance Against Japanese Aggression and the historical fact that Taiwan was restored to China after being freed from Japan's colonial rule. Instead, he has used the term "the end of the war," favored by Japanese right-wing forces, in place of references to Japan's defeat in the war. Lai's speech also contained statements that stoked confrontation across the Strait rather than promoting reconciliation. He pledged to continue military reforms, strengthen asymmetric warfare capabilities and increase military spending, while claiming that these measures were intended to deter war rather than provoke it. But such rhetoric cannot conceal his true colors as a saboteur of peace, a maker of crises and an instigator of war. The worsening of cross-Strait relations since the secessionist-minded Democratic Progressive Party came to power in 2016 demonstrates that secessionist moves in pursuit of "Taiwan independence" pose the greatest threat to peace and stability across the Strait. Since taking office, Lai has established a so-called Whole-of-Society Defense Resilience Committee, constantly conducted military exercises and civil-military integrated drills, designated numerous civilian facilities as purported wartime response centers, expanded military spending, and stepped up arms purchases from external sources. These moves have heightened cross-Strait tensions and exposed Taiwan to greater security risks. Lai's stubborn adherence to secessionism runs counter to the Taiwan people's aspirations for peace, development, and cross-Strait exchanges and cooperation. It also disregards the broader interests of the Chinese nation. No matter how he repackages his rhetoric or disguises his intentions, the secessionist agenda behind his words remains evident. Reunification is an inevitable historical trend. Attempts to pursue "Taiwan independence," including through military means, lead nowhere. People on both sides of the Taiwan Strait share fundamental interests in peace, stability and development. People in Taiwan should join their fellow Chinese on the mainland in opposing secessionism, upholding peace and stability across the Strait, and advancing the cause of national reunification. item.title: China's trade strength rooted in competitiveness, not currency depreciation
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-11
China's trade strength rooted in competitiveness, not currency depreciation This photo taken on Oct. 19, 2023 shows the People's Bank of China in Beijing, capital of China. (Xinhua/Peng Ziyang) BEIJING, Oct. 10 (Xinhua) -- China has reaffirmed its stance on its foreign exchange policy amid increased discussions over the yuan's valuation, as solid facts and figures support the view that the country's export strength is rooted in its industrial competitiveness rather than currency valuation. China has neither the need nor the intention to gain trade advantages through currency devaluation, the People's Bank of China (PBOC) said in a policy statement released on Thursday, stressing that the country has never resorted to competitive devaluation. The statement came as some countries pointed to currency valuation as a cause of trade imbalances, thereby oversimplifying the dynamics between exchange rates and trade. The conventional view that currency appreciation weakens export competitiveness largely reflects a short-term and static perspective. Over a longer horizon, competitiveness is shaped by much more than exchange rates, analysts have said. This is particularly evident in China's case. The international competitiveness of Chinese products has at times continued to strengthen even as the RMB appreciated. From 2020 to 2021, the RMB appreciated by about 9 percent against the U.S. dollar, while China's share of global exports increased by 1.7 percentage points in this period, according to the PBOC. In 2022, by contrast, the RMB depreciated by more than 8 percent against the dollar, while China's share of global exports fell by 0.7 percentage points, PBOC said. These figures showed that China's imports and exports are relatively insensitive to exchange-rate movements, while neither its goods trade surplus nor its current-account surplus has a simple linear relationship with the RMB exchange rate, said Guan Tao, chief economist at Huafu Securities Co., Ltd. Attributing China's export strength primarily to currency depreciation or other purported factors including "overcapacity" reflects a fundamental misunderstanding of the sophistication and competitiveness of the country's industrial sector. At its core, China's trade growth is underpinned by its vast domestic market, comprehensive industrial and supply chains, well-developed infrastructure, abundant and highly skilled workforce, and steadily improving research and innovation capabilities, the central bank noted. Dong Ximiao, chief economist at China Merchants Union Consumer Finance, said that historically, the world's major trade surplus countries have generally been those with strong industrial competitiveness. For deficit economies, their deeper challenges lie in structural factors such as low savings rates, high consumption and insufficient industrial competitiveness, issues that cannot be resolved simply by focusing on the exchange rates of their trading partners. "Declining trade competitiveness in some countries reflects their own structural difficulties," said Hao Yubiao, director of the National Center for Economic Security Studies at Capital University of Economics and Business. "Pointing the finger at other countries' currency exchange rates amounts to avoiding the need for domestic adjustment and does little to solve the underlying problems." At a time when currencies in neighboring countries have been depreciating, China has refrained from pursuing beggar-thy-neighbor policies or competitive devaluation. This year, both the onshore and offshore RMB have strengthened past the 6.7 mark against the U.S. dollar. China had never resorted to competitive currency devaluation to boost exports to offset intensive external shocks in the past, the central bank said. Over the past two decades, the RMB has experienced multiple cycles of appreciation and depreciation, reflecting increasingly pronounced two-way movements and greater exchange-rate flexibility. The PBOC said that looking ahead, both appreciation and depreciation factors remain in play and that the future direction of the RMB exchange rates remains uncertain. Such two-way fluctuations are consistent with China's efforts to make the exchange rate more flexible and market-oriented. As a responsible major economy, China has also been committed to addressing such trade imbalances via international cooperation. At a meeting of G20 finance ministers and central bank governors last month, PBOC Governor Pan Gongsheng said structural reforms are needed across economies to address global trade imbalances. He called on deficit economies to reduce fiscal deficits and raise domestic savings rates, while surplus economies should appropriately promote growth in consumption and investment. Countries should formulate medium- and long-term policy plans, make clear commitments and follow through on those commitments, Pan said. Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. All Rights Reserved.

item.title: Descendants of Doolittle Raid participants visit Shangrao, China's Jiangxi
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-11
Descendants of Doolittle Raid participants visit Shangrao, China's Jiangxi A descendant of a rescued Doolittle Raid participant (R) hugs a descendant of a Chinese villager who took part in the rescue in Shangrao, east China's Jiangxi Province, Oct. 10, 2026. The Doolittle Raid, planned and led by U.S. Lieutenant Colonel James Doolittle on April 18, 1942, was an air raid on Japan as a retaliation for the attack on the U.S. Pearl Harbor. After the raid, 15 planes heading for an airport in Quzhou ran out of fuel and crashed in various localities in east China. Chinese villagers risked their lives to rescue the parachuting airmen and helped them evacuate to safety. Of the 75 airmen aboard the planes, 64 were rescued by the Chinese people. However, many locals were suspected of sheltering the Americans, and some were tortured or even killed by Japanese soldiers. In China, the Doolittle story has long been regarded as a symbol of the friendship forged between the Chinese and American peoples during their joint fight against fascism. On Oct. 10, 6 representatives of descendants of the Doolittle Raid participants visited Shangrao to view a historical exhibition, revisit rescue sites and pay tribute to the Chinese people who rescued American airmen 84 years ago.
